about: The Rational family (arts/gen/src/gen/Rational.kt). One entry per style: the file prefix is rational<name>, variants are 01, 02, ... in order. Used by sheet.mjs and review.mjs for captions.

styles.name: Modules
styles.description: Bauhaus tiles. Each tile reads the four Gaussian integers at its corners: one prime grows a quarter disc, two adjacent a half disc, two opposite two small quarters, three a disc, four an accent disc.

styles.name: Lattice
styles.description: The Gaussian primes themselves, one mark per prime. Centred on 0 they keep their eightfold symmetry; the axis primes take the accent.

styles.name: Overlay
styles.description: Overprinted fields, small blocks, a bar and a disc on a 12-column grid, placed and sized by the primes nearest a seeded point. Printed grain on every fill.

styles.name: Score
styles.description: Ruled lines with a mark for every run of consecutive primes along each line, the longest run in the accent, bar lines every eight steps.

styles.name: Nest
styles.description: Squares nested into a corner, each band stippled denser than the last, band widths from successive prime norms.

styles.name: Arcs
styles.description: Truchet tiles: two quarter-arc bands per tile join its edge midpoints. A tile turns when the primality of its corner and the one diagonally across differ, so the bands run on into long curves.

styles.name: Orbit
styles.description: One ring per Gaussian prime norm, evenly spaced, with a mark at the true argument of every prime of that norm: eight to a ring, four on the axes in the accent.

styles.name: Division
styles.description: De Stijl: the square cut again and again on a grid, the direction, place and depth of every cut read from a stream of primes.

styles.name: Halftone
styles.description: A dot screen over the odd sub-lattice. A prime is a full dot, anything else is sized by its prime neighbours, and the tone fades across the image so it can sit behind text.

styles.name: Stripes
styles.description: Swiss-poster forms filled with a barcode read off one row of the lattice: a band for every prime, a hairline for every composite, the longest run in the accent.
variants: field with a disc cut out, grain

styles.name: Journey
styles.description: The Truchet arcs as fine lines, and the longest open path through them, edge to edge, as a wide accent band with a dot at each end.

styles.name: Rounds
styles.description: Square frames, each the last one shrunk toward a point the primes pick, stippled denser round by round, ending on a solid accent square.

styles.name: Versions
styles.description: A contact sheet of nine panels, each the same window of Bauhaus tiles moved one step along the lattice, so shapes walk from panel to panel. The last panel, the one kept, is in the accent.

styles.name: Drafts
styles.description: The same square laid down again and again in translucent grain, each draft nearer the final place, the final one in the accent.

styles.name: Parts
styles.description: Truchet tiles pulled apart into separate pieces, each in a hairline slot. A few lift out of their slots, the first in the accent.

styles.name: Assembly
styles.description: A De Stijl division whose cells hold parts fitted to their shape: a disc, a quarter from a corner, a half on the long side, a solid or stippled block.

styles.name: Tree
styles.description: Rows of a file tree, indented as the primes along each lattice row say. Folders are squares, files discs, each with a bar for its name; the deepest file, the new component, is in the accent.

styles.name: Kit
styles.description: A specimen sheet of the parts, a family to a row (discs, halves, quarters, blocks), each in a hairline cell. The primes turn each row, stipple some parts and pick the one accent.

styles.name: Pulse
styles.description: A row of bars like a waveform, each as tall as the double diamond is at that point, scaled by how prime its lattice neighbourhood is. An accent dot holds the pinch.

styles.name: Fan
styles.description: Strings that open from a point and close on the next, twice. Each diamond keeps the candidate strings whose lattice point is prime, with a node where each turns; the meeting point is the accent.

styles.name: Branches
styles.description: A bracket that splits one into two into four and joins back, twice, in square elbows. Prime nodes are discs, the rest small squares; the single middle node is the accent.

styles.name: Rhombs
styles.description: Two lozenges overprinted in grain on a ruled axis, overlapping where one phase hands over to the next, the axis ticked at every prime along a lattice row, an accent square where they meet.

styles.name: Twin
styles.description: A halftone over the true odd lattice whose tone is the double diamond: dots swell toward each diamond's centre and are gone outside. Primes are full dots.

styles.name: Knots
styles.description: Truchet arcs only inside the double diamond, the band swelling toward each diamond's centre, so the curves gather into two knots joined at the pinch.
